tour.title: Guided Tour
tour.description: Fly through the solar system and beyond

sun.name: The Sun
sun.narration: Our star, the Sun, contains 99.8% of the solar system's mass. Its gravity holds everything in orbit.

mercury.name: Mercury
mercury.narration: Closest to the Sun, Mercury has extreme temperatures from -180°C to 430°C. A year here is just 88 Earth days.

venus.name: Venus
venus.narration: Earth's 'twin' in size, but with a crushing CO2 atmosphere and surface temperatures hot enough to melt lead.

earth.name: Earth
earth.narration: Our home, the only known world with liquid water on its surface and life. The Moon stabilizes our climate.

mars.name: Mars
mars.narration: The Red Planet, once wet and warm. Now a cold desert with the largest volcano and canyon in the solar system.

asteroidBelt.name: Asteroid Belt
asteroidBelt.narration: Between Mars and Jupiter, millions of rocky remnants from the solar system's formation orbit the Sun.

jupiter.name: Jupiter
jupiter.narration: The king of planets. Its Great Red Spot is a storm larger than Earth, raging for at least 350 years.

saturn.name: Saturn
saturn.narration: Famous for its spectacular rings made of ice and rock. Saturn could float in water—it's less dense than water!

uranus.name: Uranus
uranus.narration: An ice giant tilted on its side, rolling through the solar system. Its blue-green color comes from methane.

neptune.name: Neptune
neptune.narration: The windiest world, with supersonic winds over 2,000 km/h. Its deep blue hides a hot, dense core.

edgeOfSolarSystem.name: Edge of the Solar System
edgeOfSolarSystem.narration: Beyond Neptune lies the Kuiper Belt and the heliopause—where the Sun's influence ends and interstellar space begins.

milkyWay.name: The Milky Way
milkyWay.narration: Our home galaxy, a barred spiral of 100–400 billion stars. We're in the Orion Arm, 27,000 light-years from the center.
